title: Nano-formulations in treatment of iron deficiency anaemia: An overview - ScienceDirect

Researchers found that the particle size of active forms play a crucial role in permeation through biological membranes which promote effective iron absorption [44]. In that same context, nanoparticular systems have shown increased usefulness in iron absorption and uptake by enhanced system characteristics such as controlled release patterns, solubility in different pH and permeability of iron formulations through the GIT, thereby making iron bioavailability more effective.
Moreover, iron is poorly absorbed orally due to its narrow absorption window, mainly from the duodenum and proximal jejunum, leading to a considerable variation in the bioavailability of different iron dosage forms [14]. Recently, there has been a surge in the development of nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems to improve oral bioavailability [15]. Novel drug delivery systems are reported to treat IDA, including synthesized polymeric nanoparticles of iron and other nanoparticles obtained from magnetite and folic acid [16]. Ferrous and ferric iron supplements are the two types of supplemental iron available.
Iron citrate complexes are a promising example. Citric acid enhances iron absorption, and ferric citrate has already been proven to ensure high bioavailability [14]. Over the years, authors have also tried to synthesize a citric acid-iron(II) complex [15–17].
Iron deficiency anaemia (IDA) is a significant challenge to global health. The absorption and bioavailability depend on the delivery vehicle being used. Ferrous sulphate is a drug of choice for IDA but leads to frequent gastrointestinal tract side effects that force the patient to discontinue the treatment.
